cases.name: Validate duplicate-key joins
cases.prompt: Join orders to customer_status by customer_id. Some customer_status rows are duplicated. The output has more rows than orders. Review the code and propose a safe fix.
cases.description: Diagnose row multiplication caused by duplicate join keys and make the data-quality decision explicit.
traps: Assume left_join always preserves row count

assertions.text: Explains many-to-one or many-to-many row multiplication
Checks duplicate keys on the right table
Uses relationship validation or an explicit data-quality decision

cases.name: Control grouped summaries
cases.prompt: Write a grouped summary of mean revenue by region and channel, excluding missing revenue, then ensure a later ungrouped mutate is not affected by retained groups.
cases.description: Build a grouped summary with an explicit missing-value policy and predictable grouping lifecycle.

assertions.text: Controls grouping with .groups or explicit ungroup
Produces one summary row per intended group

cases.name: Program column-wise transformations
cases.prompt: A function receives a character vector of numeric column names and should standardize only those columns. Make the interface robust when one requested name is absent.
cases.description: Use tidy evaluation and column-wise operations safely when column names arrive as strings.
traps: Use all_of when absence should be tolerated

assertions.text: Uses any_of for intentionally optional names
Uses across or an equivalent column-wise operation
Restricts the transformation to numeric columns or validates types
Keeps the string-driven interface distinct from data-masked input
